Interface Rational


  • public interface Rational
    A Rational has:
    • an int numerator
    • a non-zero int denominator
    Version:
    20244129-10:41:04
    Author:

      • add

        Rational add(Rational r)
        Returns a new Rational number that represents the sum of this Rational number and r. This sum follows the Mathematics rule for addition of fractions except there is no reduction to lowest terms. Thus <1,2>.add(<3,4>) == <(1*4 + 3*2), 2*4> == <10,8>, NOT <5,4>.
        Parameters:
        r - Rational to add to this Rational.
        Returns:
        sum of this Rational and r

      • mult

        Rational mult(Rational r)
        Returns a new Rational number that represents the product of this Rational number and r. The resulting product is a Rational number whose numerator is the product of this Rational's numerator and r's numerator, while the product's denominator is the product of this Rational's denominator and r's denominator.
        Parameters:
        r - Rational by which this Rational is multiplied
        Returns:
        product of this Rational and r

      • toString

        java.lang.String toString()
        Returns the state string for this Rational. The returned string is of the format "<n,d>" where n is the numerator and d is the denominator.
        Overrides:
        toString in class java.lang.Object
        Returns:
        state string

      • equals

        boolean equals(java.lang.Object o)
        Returns true if o is equal to this Rational. Note that o can't be null, must be assignable to Rational (i.e., o must be a Rational or an implementation of Rational), and all of its fields must match those of this Rational.
        Overrides:
        equals in class java.lang.Object
        Parameters:
        o - object to test for equality to this Rational
        Returns:
        true if o is equal to this Rational
